source_row.wylie: mthar thug ni, sbyor ba de'i rkyen gyis pha rol po de'i tshe'am, dus gzhan gyi tshe shi ba'o, , de yang mdzod las, snga dang mnyam du shi ba la, , dngos med lus gzhan skyes phyir ro, , zhes gsungs pa ni 'dir yang 'dra'o
source_row.english: The conclusion occurs when, due to this undertaking of the deed, the other person dies, either at the time of the undertaking, or later on. As the Treasure House of Knowledge says, There is no actual stage for those who die Before or together, for another body's been born. *********

spans.rationale: The established completion term directly attests conclusion and identifies the final component.
The causal undertaking noun owns the first English undertaking, not its later anaphoric repetition in the time phrase.
This demonstrative points to that undertaking and is placed before it in English; its bound genitive stays outside.
The complete causal expression directly attests due to. RKYEN remains with the intact GYIS, without splitting an agentive suffix.
The established other-person expression denotes the victim whose death completes the act. The article remains unwrapped.

spans.eng: at the time of the undertaking, or
spans.rationale: The full temporal/disjunctive construction is expanded as this complete English time phrase. DE'I resumes the already named undertaking, TSHE supplies time, and bound AM supplies or. The repeated undertaking is an anaphoric expansion of DE, not a second claim on SBYOR BA; either remains outside.
The established other-time compound directly attests later on. Its temporal continuation GYI TSHE is not falsely assigned a second English time.
The complete first death predicate retains its bound sentence ending and owns dies in the victim clause. It is distinct from the later quoted die.
The abbreviated source title has direct glossary support for the complete English work title. It is preserved whole without an invented knowledge member.
The prior-death qualifier belongs to the quotation. Its capital is preserved as lineation, not an English proper name.
This conjunction coordinates the alternative before/together cases and is rendered or. It cannot reuse the earlier temporal or.
The complete adverbial lexical expression directly attests together and supplies simultaneous death. Neither MNYAM nor DU is duplicated within it.
The second death predicate owns quoted die, distinct from the first prose dies.
The case particle relates the absence of the actual stage to those dying before or together. It owns the first for in the quote, not the reason marker before another body.
The actual-stage term is abbreviated to DNGOS in the verse. The direct actual gloss is retained tightly; explanatory stage is left outside.
The negative existential denies that actual stage for the specified cases. Full MED evidence supports there-is-no constructions; no negative morpheme or supplied personal subject is invented.

The body noun owns body before the apostrophe in the printed contraction body's. The apostrophe-s means has and is English auxiliary support, not part of a Tibetan possessive; it remains unwrapped without a subword override.
The other/new body is rendered another. This local modifier is distinct from the earlier other-person compound. The unrelated auto-aligned a bodhisattva gloss is not promoted.
The birth verb owns born, excluding the English perfect/passive auxiliary wording.
The actual source here is PHYIR and supplies the causal for. The earlier C05:343 verse writes PHYER; its registered spelling question does not alter this correct current source form.

spans.nul: Complete RO closes the quoted birth proposition at the period after born. Full particle evidence supports this punctuation fusion. The following asterisk separator does not supply a lexical exponent, and this null does not cover the separate omitted concluding Tibetan application phrase.

omissions.tib: ni; first bound genitive; gyi tshe after dus gzhan; de yang; las after mdzod; zhes; final ni 'dir yang 'dra'o
omissions.reason: Topic, temporal continuation, citation and concluding application are compressed in the English prose and As-the-book-says frame. The final here-too-is-the-same statement has no separate matching English phrase; it may be conveyed by applying the quotation in this frame or omitted in the published excerpt. Leave that unresolved scope unbanked, not null, and do not claim the asterisks translate it.

omissions.reason: Articles, temporal and citation framing, repeated deed wording, generic participants, the nominal stage explanation and English auxiliaries stay unwrapped. Asterisks are physical source apparatus, not Tibetan lexical content. The exact later time phrase is supported by its demonstrative construction rather than reuse of the first undertaking token.
